title: Does Merge Form a Hopf Algebra? Coproducts, Traces, and the Prospects of Algebraic Minimalism
abstract: arXiv:2611.11502v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Marcolli, Chomsky, and Berwick (2025; henceforth MCB) formulate the Merge operation of Minimalism on a Hopf algebra of Connes-Kreimer type, and claim that language and physics obey the same algebraic structure. This paper examines the premise of that claim: whether Merge on workspaces can be described as a Hopf algebra. We first survey five coproducts for coassociativity and a connected grading: the Connes-Kreimer coproduct $\Delta_\rho$, MCB's two coproducts $\Delta_d$ and $\Delta_c$, the contraction coproduct of Marcolli and Skigin (2025), and the coproduct of Xiao (2026). $\Delta_d$ is not coassociative. For $\Delta_c$, MCB gives no rule for the labels of trace leaves in trees that already contain trace leaves; under the literal extension it is not coassociative, but once a rule and a grading are supplied it yields a graded connected Hopf algebra. translated_title: 《Merge能构成霍普夫代数吗？余积、语迹与代数极简主义的前景》
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.11502v2（更正公告）。摘要：Marcolli、Chomsky与Berwick（2025，下文简称MCB）在Connes-Kreimer型的霍普夫代数上为极简主义的Merge操作建立了形式化表述，并声称语言与物理遵循相同的代数结构。本文检验了这一主张的前提：工作区上的Merge能否被描述为一个霍普夫代数。我们首先从余结合性与连通分次的角度考察了五个候选余积：Connes-Kreimer余积Δ_ρ、MCB的两个余积Δ_d与Δ_c、Marcolli与Skigin（2025）的收缩余积，以及Xiao（2026）的余积。结果表明：Δ_d不是余结合的；对于Δ_c，MCB并未给出在已含语迹叶子的树中如何标记语迹叶子标签的规则，按字面推广该余积不是余结合的，但一旦补充相应规则与分次，它便给出一个分次连通的霍普夫代数；Xiao的余积是余结合的，而Marcolli与Skigin的余积在……（摘要原文在此处截断）同样是余结合的。
tldr: 本文检验了“Merge能否构成霍普夫代数”这一代数极简主义的核心数学前提，通过对五个候选余积的余结合性与连通分次分析发现：MCB的Δ_d不满足余结合性，Δ_c需补充语迹标记规则与分次后才能给出分次连通霍普夫代数，而Xiao与Marcolli-Skigin的余积则是余结合的。
en_tdlr: This paper tests the core premise of algebraic Minimalism—whether Merge can form a Hopf algebra—and, through an analysis of five candidate coproducts, finds that MCB's Δ_d is not coassociative, that Δ_c yields a graded connected Hopf algebra only once a trace-labeling rule and grading are supplied, and that the coproducts of Xiao and of Marcolli-Skigin are coassociative.
